claims.text: This trip's GPS trace measures 30.89 km from the recorded pickup event to the recorded dropoff event against a platform optimal of 22.1 km — an excess of 8.79 km, or 39.8% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and it is established on this trip's own trace.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, because the trip record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. The rider therefore measures on the trace figure — 30.89 km, not the rounded 30.9 km — and the excess of 8.79 km clears both thresholds on the governing field.

The excess of 8.79 km is additionally greater than 8.0 km in absolute terms, so POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation and not merely an established one. The rider does not need to characterise the trip to get there; the derived status reads straight off the trace.

The driver's own account concedes the route change: 'There was heavy fog on the SLE that morning so I went around.' The trace shows exactly that — 30.89 km driven where the platform's route was 22.1 km. The fact of the detour is therefore common ground, and the only live question is whether any clause in the policy excuses it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00505, and the GPS first fix at 05:46:40 matches the recorded start on the trip record. The excess measured from an unimpaired trace meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden has shifted to the driver, who must now point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and a general assertion that traffic was bad will not do it.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 217 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no 500 m jump, no sampling interval above 30 seconds — so no corroboration beyond the trace is required, the deviation may stand on the trace alone, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

The driver's fog explanation is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00505-01 is MISSING — no payload, admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no advisory names the SLE or any segment the optimal route traverses, no validity window exists to compare against the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record. Under POL-RD-08 an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge the driver's burden, and under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure with POL-RD-02 running against the booked optimal route. Because the driver has cited no advisory identifier, the absent artifact is a gap in the bundle and not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. The rider discloses that this claim rests on a weight-0.0 artifact, and rests on it precisely because its absence is citable.

None of the driver-favouring exculpatory routes is open on this record. The chat log for the trip is empty — message_count 0, no messages, not truncated — so there is no rider instruction that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-price against. And the vehicle type is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, with solo_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. Nothing is left to reduce the measured excess.

POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route here: fare_model on the fare breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip and the rider is not already whole on distance and time. The POL-RD-02 recomputation therefore runs in the ordinary way.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic is fixed by the ledger and by the policy constants, not by discretion. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 27.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 28.7350. charged_total is 37.86, so the refund is 9.1250, well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, rounded UP to SGD 9.15 payable. That is 24.1% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome for the filing party is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15.

There is no pass-through correction to add and no risk of double-counting one. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines at all — the erp_gantries list is empty and the on-route and off-route totals are both 0.00 — and there is no airport surcharge, which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there. The POL-RD-02 refund is therefore the whole of the rider's monetary remedy, with nothing to settle separately under POL-RD-09.

POL-RD-06's check is triggered by the material deviation, and the rider reads its citable counters honestly rather than stretching them: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, so no deviation pattern is established on the fields the clause names. The rider accordingly claims neither the FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c), and asks only for the POL-RD-02 partial. No other field on the driver profile is relied on, because POL-GEN-01 confines the citable counters to those the clause names.

The corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 does not bite on this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4 or more, so no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required to sustain a claim with an excess below 30% or above it. The rider cites that field only because POL-RD-08 names it, and cites no other field on the rider profile, per POL-GEN-01.

The fare stands at payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider is today carrying the whole SGD 37.86. A PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-RD-02 returns SGD 9.15 to the filing party; NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute would leave the charge exactly where it is, which is why the present state standing is not a rider-favourable outcome.

The rider does not press the SGD 210 rebooking fee as part of this claim. The route-deviation policy makes the remedy arithmetic against the fare lines under POL-RD-02, and the contested amount before this tribunal is the fare of SGD 37.86; a missed check-in is not a line the policy refunds, and the rider concedes that rather than ask for a remedy the policy does not provide.

claims.text: On this trip's own trace the driven distance is 30.89 km against a booked optimal of 22.1 km, an excess of 8.79 km (39.77%) — the POL-RD-01 threshold is passed on both limbs, over 20% and over 0.8 km, so the driver does not dispute that a deviation is established on the trace. What is disputed is the remedy, and the policy fixes that arithmetically rather than at the figures the rider names.

The POL-RD-02 refund is charged_total less the recomputed optimal-route fare: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 27.0) x surge_multiplier 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee = 28.735; so the refund before rounding is 37.86 less 28.735 = 9.125, and the payable figure rounds UP to SGD 9.15. That is the entirety of the rider's monetary remedy on this trip.

The refund of 9.125 is 24.10% of the 37.86 charged_total and does not reach the 90% full-refund share, so POL-RD-02 compels a PARTIAL_REFUND and never a FULL_REFUND: the driver keeps the 28.735 that reflects the optimal route and the rider is returned 9.15.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so the POL-RD-06 uplift and referral do not fire: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250, a ratio of 0 against the 0.05 test and a count below the 3-flag test. Even the marginal materiality of this excess — 8.79 km against the 8.0 km limb and 39.77% against the 50% limb — cannot turn a first flagged trip into a pattern, and POL-RD-06 forbids using any other profile field for the test.

Nothing is added on the pass-through lines: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and an airport_surcharge of 0.00, which is the correct treatment for a trip whose dropoff is Changi T1 but which does not originate there. POL-RD-09 also forbids adding any off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, because it is already comprehended in that figure — so no standalone correction is due.

The SGD 210 rebooking fee, and the rider's demand for the whole fare, has no footing in the loaded policy: POL-RD-02 makes the route-deviation remedy arithmetic on the fare lines and caps it at charged_total, and no clause of POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION or POLICY-GENERAL provides for a missed flight or a rebooking charge. The amount contested on the record is 37.86, and the remedy computed on that sum is 9.15.

The driver's fog account does not exonerate him and the driver's advocate does not press it: the only traffic_advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00505-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (no advisory covers the SLE or TPE in this window), so POL-RD-03's test — a named road the optimal route traverses, an overlapping validity window, and a route that leaves and rejoins the corridor — cannot be run at all, and an uncited traffic assertion discharges no burden under POL-RD-08. The consequence is the ordinary POL-RD-02 figure, not the rider's.

The case is decidable and should be ruled rather than held: the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because the driver cited no advisory identifier for it and POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion citing no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against one (EV-ADVIS-00505-01 is cited here for its absence only — MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — and carries no fact). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 217 fixes, 100% coverage, a 10-second cadence and max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is not met and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. The disputed amount should be settled at 9.15, not frozen.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this is a metered RYDE_PLUS trip from Yishun to Changi T1 on 24 Aug 2026, contested on a charged_total of SGD 37.86. The GPS trace measures 30.89 km driven against a booked optimal of 22.1 km — an excess of 8.79 km, 39.77% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), and because the excess also exceeds 8.0 km the deviation is additionally MATERIAL, which required the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check. That check was run on the fields the clause names: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift nor the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral fires.

Driver: your fog account is not evidence on this record. The only traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00505-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers the SLE or the TPE in this window. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run: there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, no validity window to compare against the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, and no leave-and-rejoin match to test. Under POL-RD-08 an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge your burden, and under POL-RD-13(2) the deviation stands at the measured figure with POL-RD-02 running against the booked optimal. Because you cited no advisory identifier, the absent artifact is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case is ruled rather than held. Nothing else in the driver-favouring clauses is open: the chat log is empty (message_count 0, no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04), pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null (no POL-RD-05 amendment to re-price against), and the vehicle is RYDE_PLUS with solo_optimal_distance_km null, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12 does not apply). The trace itself is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 217 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second cadence, gaps list empty and max_gap_sec 0.0 — so no corroboration beyond the trace was required.

Rider: the money is arithmetic, not discretionary. fare_model on the fare breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route and POL-RD-02 runs in the ordinary way. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 27.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 28.7350. The refund is charged_total 37.86 less 28.7350 = 9.1250, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and rounds UP to SGD 9.15. That is 24.1% of charged_total, well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND and not FULL_REFUND; the driver keeps the 28.7350 that reflects the optimal route. There is nothing to add on the pass-through lines: the fare carries no ERP gantries at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and an airport_surcharge of 0.00, which is correct for a trip that ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 figure because it is already comprehended in it. Your SGD 210 rebooking fee and your demand for the whole fare are not recoverable: POL-RD-02 makes the route-deviation remedy arithmetic on the fare lines and caps it at charged_total, no clause of POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION or POLICY-GENERAL provides for a missed flight, and the contested amount before this tribunal is the SGD 37.86 fare. Your rider profile was consulted only on the field POL-RD-08 names — deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required and no other profile field was used.

On confidence: the deciding facts — the excess and the fare recomputation — are carried by EV-GPS-00505, EV-TRIP-00505 and EV-FARE-00505, all at weight_multiplier 1.0. EV-ADVIS-00505-01 carries no fact at weight 0.0 and is cited only for the citable fact of its absence, so it does not depress the cap. No monetary outcome or referral arises under POL-RD-09(4), POL-RD-06(c), POL-NS-05(ii) or POL-NS-07, so the referrals list is empty.

Result: SGD 9.15 is returned to the rider; the balance of SGD 28.7350 of the fare stands, and the amount held pending any escalation is released to this ruling.

To the rider: your refund is SGD 9.15. Your trip's GPS trace records 30.89 km driven between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a platform optimal of 22.1 km — an excess of 8.79 km, or 39.8% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 tests (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) and also the 8.0 km absolute limb, so this is a material route deviation established on this trip's own trace. POL-RD-02 then makes the remedy arithmetic: ((SGD 3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 22.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 27.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + SGD 0.80 platform fee = SGD 28.735 recomputed. The charged total was SGD 37.86, so the refund before rounding is SGD 9.125, payable as SGD 9.15 (rounded up to the nearest 0.05, and well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis). That is 24.1% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome for you is a partial refund and the remaining SGD 28.71 of the charge stands. Your SGD 210 rebooking fee and your request for the whole fare are refused: no clause of the route-deviation policy or of the general policy provides for a missed flight or an airline rebooking, and the remedy is fixed arithmetically against the fare lines and capped at the fare itself. The driver's point that a missed check-in is a matter between you and the airline matches this. To the driver: the excess is not reduced by your account that heavy fog on the SLE made you go around. EV-ADVIS-00505-01, the traffic advisory for this trip, is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no advisory names a road the optimal route uses and there is no validity window to compare; POL-RD-03 cannot be run. You cited no advisory identifier yourself, so under POL-RD-13 the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and the case is decided rather than escalated. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 217 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second cadence and no gap over 90 seconds, so no corroboration beyond the trace is needed. Your statement is accepted only as an admission that a detour occurred; the finding itself rests on the trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown, all at weight 1.0. Because the deviation is material, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check was run and no pattern is established — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days — so there is no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral. The fare is METERED, not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. There are no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge to correct under POL-RD-09 (the trip ends at Changi rather than originating there, so no surcharge is due), so nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and nothing is double-counted. No compensation is payable to you: you were billed 30.9 km against 30.89 km traced, so there is no unbilled distance. Both advocates' arithmetic agrees with the ruling above; the rider's claims that the deviation is established and that the fog account fails are accepted, and the only claim rejected on its merits is the rider's demand for the SGD 210 rebooking fee.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: you are partly right, and you are owed SGD 9.15 — not the whole SGD 37.86, and not the SGD 210 you spent rebooking. Here is why, figure by figure.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS MATERIAL. The governing measurement under POL-RD-01 is the trace, not the trip record's rounded copy. EV-GPS-00505 records 30.89 km between the pickup and dropoff events, against a platform optimal of 22.1 km on EV-TRIP-00505: an excess of 8.79 km, or 39.77% of optimal. Both establishment limbs pass (over 20%, and over 0.8 km), so the deviation stands on this trip's own trace. Because the excess also exceeds 8.0 km in absolute terms, POL-RD-01 additionally records a MATERIAL deviation, and the driver-profile check that a material deviation requires has been run.

THE FOG EXPLANATION IS DISCARDED. The driver's account — heavy fog on the SLE, so he went around — is tested by POL-RD-13 against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else, and that comparison cannot be run: EV-ADVIS-00505-01 is MISSING, with no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I name it as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: it carries no fact, its absence is what is citable, and its weight of 0.0 does not enter the confidence calculation because nothing decides this case by it. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion of bad traffic that cites no advisory artifact discharges no burden. The driver did not cite the missing advisory's identifier, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged — the case is ruled, not held.

WHAT WOULD HAVE REDUCED THE EXCESS DOES NOT EXIST HERE. The chat log EV-CHAT-00505 is empty (0 messages, not truncated), so there is no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04; no amendment timestamps are set on the trip record, so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-price; and the vehicle is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. Nothing reduces the 8.79 km.

THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02). The fare is METERED, not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.1 km + 0.28 x 27.0 min) x 1.0 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 28.735. charged_total is 37.86. Refund = 37.86 - 28.735 = 9.125, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share, and is rounded UP to SGD 9.15.

PASS-THROUGH LINES (POL-RD-09): there is nothing to add or deduct. No ERP gantries were charged (erp_gantries empty, tolls 0.00) and no airport surcharge applies, correctly, because this trip ends at Changi rather than originating there. No off-route ERP is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, because it is already comprehended in it.

NO DRIVER UPLIFT AND NO CONDUCT REFERRAL (POL-RD-06): deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in the trailing 90 days — no pattern is established, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the driver-conduct referral fires. No other profile field was used for any finding. No billing-integrity referral arises either, as no charge line is unmatched.

THE SGD 210 REBOOKING FEE AND THE FULL-FARE DEMAND ARE REJECTED. No clause of POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION or POLICY-GENERAL provides for a missed flight or a rebooking charge; the remedy is arithmetic against the fare lines and capped at the charged total. That part of the claim fails for want of any clause to grant it.

To the driver: you keep SGD 28.735 of the fare, which reflects the optimal route you should have driven, and SGD 9.15 is returned to the rider. Your route-change account helped nobody, because there was no advisory on file to test it against. One open point for the platform's own attention, not for this ruling: the rider reports a 20-day unanswered contact timeline and the in-app chat and call records for this trip are empty — that is a service issue outside the money this ruling moves.

CONFIDENCE: the deciding facts (the trace distance and the booked optimal) are carried by EV-GPS-00505 and EV-TRIP-00505, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; the ruling sits at 0.9, above the 0.70 floor.
